chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from a slave of the Banu Hashim, from Muhammad ibn Ja'far ibn Muhammad, who said:

Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) went out one night wearing a robe of khazz and a cloak of khazz, and he had covered his beard with al-ghaliya. So they said, 'At this time and in this appearance?' He said, 'I intend to court the Houris for Allah, Mighty and Majestic, during this night.'
Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ali ibn Asbaat, from a slave of the Banu Hashim, from Muhammad ibn Ja'far — similar to it.

key_terms.الْغَالِيَةِ: Al-Ghaliya, a type of perfume or scent
key_terms.جُبَّةُ خَزٍّ: A robe made of khazz (a fine silk or wool fabric)

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of Imam Ali ibn al-Husayn wearing fine clothes and perfume at night?
ai.summary: This narration from *Al-Kafi* highlights the Shia concept of *tazayyun* (adornment) as an act of worship, where Imam Ali ibn al-Husayn (Zayn al-Abidin) utilized fine clothing and *al-ghaliya* perfume not for vanity, but to prepare his physical presence for the 'marriage' to the Houris of Paradise. The metaphor of 'courting' (*akhutb*) reflects the spiritual intimacy between the Imams and the divine, emphasizing that outward beauty, when purified by intention, serves as a means of drawing closer to Allah. This incident is often cited by scholars to validate the permissibility and virtue of using perfume and fine garments in acts of devotion.
